_comment: Tier-2 for skfem point_source#1, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: ib.zeros() gives a fresh float64 array of length ib.N and f[node]=1.0 is the right one-hot point load, while unit_load.assemble(ib) 'gives a 1.0 at every DOF' and yields a solution with 'peaks at all interior nodes'. Ran: MeshTri().refined(4), ElementTriP1, 289 DOFs, both right-hand sides solved with condense/solve, plus a Green's-function reciprocity check. Printed: the ib.zeros() half is exactly right (float64, length 289, all zero, fresh each call). BOTH unit_load claims are FALSE: unit_load holds the INTEGRAL of each basis function, ranging 6.51e-04 to 3.91e-03 and summing to the domain area 1.000000, not 1.0 per entry; and its solution is a single smooth bump with ONE interior maximum at the centre -- the same location the point-source solution peaks -- so counting peaks does not separate them. What does separate them is the peak value (0.600093 vs 0.073446). The sharp check is reciprocity: the integral of the point-source solution equals the unit-load solution AT the source to 3.8e-16 relative, because the Green's function is symmetric. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 replaces the 'ul = unit_load.assemble(ib)' right-hand side by the correct one-hot point load (ib.zeros() with 1.0 at the source DOF) -- the documented fix for using the constant-source assembly where a point source was meant. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 12 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'unit_load_entries_are_basis_integrals=True', 'point_peak_exceeds_unit_load_peak=True' and 'greens_function_reciprocity_holds=True' so the fixture goes red. Note that 'unit_load_sums_to_domain_area=True' SURVIVES, because the unit point load also totals 1.0 on this unit-area domain -- that check cannot tell the two right-hand sides apart. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
